meta.title: LUZ: a light, usable and zero-dependency design system for the web
meta.description: LUZ (Light, Usable & Zero-dependency) is a design system of tokens, CSS and a little vanilla JavaScript that starts from what the browser already does: native HTML, three color modes, one cascade layer you can always override, and no build step.

light.title: The light where you are
light.nojs: With JavaScript on, the light of your hour is drawn here.
light.fact.1: Light takes only 1.3 seconds to travel from the Moon to Earth.
light.fact.2: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach us; if the Sun went out, it would take us that long to notice.
light.fact.3: In just one second, a beam of light could travel around the Earth 7.5 times along the equator.
light.fact.4: A ‘light-year’ does not measure time, but the distance light travels in one year, which equals nearly 9.5 trillion kilometers.
light.fact.5: Due to the time light takes to travel, when you look at the stars at night you are seeing them as they were tens, hundreds, or thousands of years ago.
light.fact.6: According to current physics, the speed of light in a vacuum is the cosmic speed limit; nothing with mass can travel faster than it.
light.fact.7: Light slows down to about 225,000 km/s when traveling through water due to the density of the medium.
light.fact.8: In a laboratory, scientists managed to slow light down to just 61 kilometers per hour by passing it through extremely cold sodium.
light.fact.9: A light (or radio) signal takes between 3 and 22 minutes to reach Mars, depending on how aligned the planets are.
light.alt.globe: A globe lit by the sun as it is now, its land a puzzle with one faint grey piece for each country: the day side faces the light, the night side fades.

hero.title: LUZ, design system for humans, ready for AI.
hero.lead: Tokens, CSS and a little vanilla JavaScript, built on what the browser already does. Every component works before JavaScript loads & We love TDD, every change starts with a failing test.
why.title: Three words, one promise.
why.lead: A CSS-first, zero-build design system for the web. Your CSS always wins, JavaScript is only an enhancement, and every page works before it loads.
why.light.text: Plain CSS and small ES modules from a CDN or npm. No preprocessor, no compiler: what you read in the files is what the browser runs.
why.light.swatches: Try this page in another light
why.light.tap: Tap a light to borrow another hour.
why.usable.text: Native first: dialog, popover, details, range, progress. Keyboard support, visible focus and 4.5:1 text contrast are part of every component, not an option.
why.usable.done: That was the keyboard alone. Press Escape to close this note.
why.usable.hint: The focus ring takes the color of the page’s actions, and it never hides.
why.zero.label: runtime dependencies. Nothing to install to try it, and no framework to keep up with for years.
inside.title: Adopt it one layer at a time.
inside.lead: One direction: each package needs the ones below it and nothing above it, and installing it brings them in. Pick the level you need and stop there.
adopt.level1.title: Tokens only
adopt.level1.when: Choose this if you already have components or a framework and only want consistent values and color modes.
adopt.level1.semantic: {n:primitives} color primitives and {n:semantic} semantic tokens, the semantic ones defined for light, dark and high contrast
adopt.level1.scales: Scales for spacing, control heights, type sizes, radii and shadows
adopt.level2.title: Tokens + Core
adopt.level2.when: Choose this if you are building pages or an app and bring your own page layout.
adopt.level2.components: {n:components} components, from buttons and forms to tabs and a media player, and {n:objects} layout objects
adopt.level2.layer: Everything in one cascade layer, luz: your own CSS wins without !important
adopt.level3.title: Tokens + Core + Site
adopt.level3.when: Choose this if your site needs a search, a cookie banner or more than one language. This home page is built on it.
adopt.level3.search: Site search and a cookie consent band that covers nothing, with optional JavaScript
adopt.level3.parts: A language switch, submenus for the links of a header, and a banner above it
adopt.next.title: Level 4 · one package for your kind of site
adopt.next.lead: Each is built on site. Install the one for your site: it brings everything below it.
adopt.next.landing: landing for a landing page
adopt.next.cms: cms for a blog or a newspaper
adopt.next.app: app for a web application
native.title: Starts from what the browser already does.
native.lead: Every component is a native element with a stylesheet on top. Switch JavaScript off and they still open, close, slide and choose.
native.details.text: That there is no step between the files you read and the page the browser shows. Copy them, link them, done.
native.dialog.title: A native dialog
native.dialog.text: Focus moves into it, Escape closes it, and the browser keeps the page behind it out of reach. No library wrote any of that.
native.dialog.note: It opens with no script where the browser has command; elsewhere a small script opens it.
native.popover.text: Light dismiss and the top layer, with no z-index to fight. The browser handles it.
native.popover.link: See the dropdown, built on a popover
native.range.label: Brightness
native.progress.label: Profile, 3 of 5 steps done
native.select.label: Size
modes.title: Light, dark, high contrast. And the hour.
modes.lead: Every semantic color is defined for the three modes, and the data-theme attribute switches them, on the page or on one part of it. This page adds an axis of its own: the time where you are.
modes.invoice.title: Invoice 1042
type.title: Made to be read.
type.lead: ET Book for running text and headings, self-hosted and MIT licensed. The system fonts for controls, labels and code.
type.quote: Light is the first material of a page. Everything else is placed in it.
fit.good.public: Content sites, documentation and public services that must meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
fit.good.server: Server-rendered pages and static sites, in any back-end language.
fit.good.own: Teams that want to read and own their CSS.
fit.bad.react: You need ready-made React or Vue components.
fit.bad.grid: You need a data grid, charts or a date-range picker: LUZ has none.
fit.bad.beta: You need a stable API today: LUZ is in beta, and names can still change.
start.title: One link tag per layer.
start.lead: Pick a level, copy the snippet, ship. Pin an exact version while LUZ is in beta.
start.then: Then write HTML. <button class="luz-btn"> is a button. <dialog class="luz-modal"> is a modal. That is the whole idea.
footer.privacy: The light is computed from your clock, never from your location. Your choice stays in this browser.
